Article Title: Best ever! From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at the Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

From 14 medals to 114: India's remarkable rise

India's Asian Para Games record

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Smaller contingent, bigger return

Hangzhou vs Aichi-Nagoya

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Athletics powers India's medal surge

India's leading medal-winning sports in Asian Para Games 2026

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Multiple medallists underline India's depth

Paralympic progress provides the wider context

Fourth place sets a new benchmark

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in 2026, India’s remarkable rise continued in Aichi-Nagoya as a smaller contingent surpassed its previous best, achieved 30 gold medals and secured its highest-ever finish at the continental para-sport showpiece.India’s campaign at the Asian Para Games 2026 was a triumph that few would have predicted when the size of the contingent became known. With just 167 athletes travelling to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the prospect of repeating the 100-plus medal haul achieved at Hangzhou in 2023 appeared ambitious. The previous edition had seen India send more than 300 athletes to the competition, returning with a record 108 medals after subsequent revisions to the original tally.But the Indian contingent defied expectations, producing an even bigger return with significantly fewer athletes. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place, both the highest medal tally and the best finish in the country's history at the event.The numbers tell a compelling story of progress. India improved its medal tally for the fifth consecutive edition, added to its gold-medal record and finished ahead of South Korea, which had threatened to challenge its position in the final standings.More than the record itself, the achievement highlighted how far India's para-sport movement has travelled in 16 years — from a modest 14-medal return at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a fourth-place finish among Asia's leading para-sport nations.India's progress at the Asian Para Games has been steady, with each edition bringing a new high in the overall medal tally.At Guangzhou in 2010, India won 14 medals — one gold, four silver and nine bronze — to finish 15th. The 2014 edition in Incheon brought a substantial improvement, with the country collecting 33 medals, including three gold, but remaining 15th in the standings.The breakthrough arrived at Jakarta in 2018. India's medal tally rose to 72, comprising 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, while its position improved to ninth.Hangzhou in 2023 marked another major leap. India crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time, initially returning with 111 medals before the tally was revised to 108 following a doping-related disqualification and a medal reallocation. The revised haul comprised 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze, with India eventually classified sixth.Aichi-Nagoya extended that upward trajectory. India added six medals to its revised Hangzhou total, increased its gold-medal count from 27 to 30 and climbed two places to fourth.The numbers at a glance: India's medal tally increased more than eightfold between 2010 and 2026. Its gold-medal count grew from one to 30, while its position improved from 15th to fourth.The rise has not been limited to the overall tally. India has improved its standing in three successive editions since 2014, moving from 15th to ninth, then sixth and now fourth. The 2026 result represents the culmination of a sustained upward trend rather than an isolated breakthrough.The most striking feature of India's latest performance was the efficiency with which its athletes converted participation into medals.India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.The comparison is revealing. India sent approximately 46 per cent fewer athletes than it did to Hangzhou, but its medal tally increased by nearly six per cent. The gold-medal count rose by three, the silver tally by three, and the bronze count remained unchanged.On a simple medals-per-athlete measure, India's return increased from approximately 0.35 medals per athlete in Hangzhou to 0.68 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is an aggregate comparison, not an individual success rate, since athletes can win multiple medals and the number of events and opportunities varies across sports.Nevertheless, the figures underline the scale of the achievement. A smaller squad did not merely match the previous edition's success; it established a new benchmark for Indian para-sport.Para-athletics was the backbone of India's campaign, delivering 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. That represented nearly 57 per cent of the country's overall tally and made athletics the single biggest contributor to India's fourth-place finish.Para-badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. Together, athletics and badminton accounted for 81 medals, more than 70 per cent of India's total.Swimming contributed 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze. Archery added six medals, including three gold and three silver, while shooting produced five, with two gold, two silver and one bronze.Athletics' contribution also illustrates how India's progress has accelerated. At Hangzhou, para-athletics produced 52 medals, including 16 gold, 17 silver and 19 bronze. In Aichi-Nagoya, the discipline's haul rose to 65, with six additional gold medals.Badminton's contribution was different. India won 21 medals in the sport at Hangzhou, including four gold, but finished with 16 in 2026. Instead, the substantial gains in athletics and the contributions from other sports helped compensate for the decline in badminton medals.That distinction matters: the record haul reflects both the strength of India's established medal-winning disciplines and the need to broaden its success across events in future editions.India's record was supported by athletes who delivered more than once during the competition. A total of 26 Indian athletes won multiple medals, while six athletes collected multiple gold medals, demonstrating the importance of individual excellence in a campaign involving 11 sports.Archer Sheetal Devi was among the standout performers, winning two gold medals and a silver. Her two golds came in the mixed compound and individual compound events, while the silver added to her three-medal haul.Athletics provided several other multiple gold medallists. Dilip Gavit, Nishad Kumar, Pranav Soorma and Simran Sharma each won two gold medals, while shooting contributed through Mona Agarwal, who also secured two golds.Four athletes finished with three medals apiece: Sheetal Devi in archery, Thulasimathi Murugesan in badminton, Ravi Budigina in swimming and Himanshu Nandal in swimming. Their performances illustrated how athletes winning across multiple events can make a significant difference to a country's final tally.The figures also invite comparison with Hangzhou, where 25 Indian athletes won multiple medals. The increase to 26 in 2026 was modest, but the overall tally improved despite a much smaller contingent. The result points to a campaign in which medal-winning performances were concentrated among a relatively small squad.India's rise at the Asian Para Games has coincided with a significant improvement at the Paralympics, strengthening the country's standing in international para-sport.At Rio 2016, India won four medals and finished 43rd. Tokyo 2020 marked a breakthrough, with 19 medals — five gold, eight silver and six bronze — lifting India to 24th. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best Paralympic haul of 29 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.The progression at the Paralympics mirrors the broader trend at the Asian Para Games: larger medal returns, more gold medals and improvements in the standings.India's able-bodied contingent had also finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games, although its 85-medal tally was below the 106 medals achieved at Hangzhou in 2023. The para contingent's performance offered a contrasting story of growth, with its medal count rising and its position improving.China dominated Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 435 medals, including 207 gold. Hosts Japan were second with 186 medals, while Uzbekistan finished third with 145. India placed fourth with 114, ahead of South Korea, which collected 100 medals, including 29 gold.India's final position was not guaranteed until the closing stages. South Korea remained within reach, but its final-day return of one gold and two silver left it one gold behind India. The Indian contingent held on to fourth place with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.The gap to third-placed Uzbekistan shows that further progress will require India to expand its medal-winning strength across disciplines. Yet the immediate achievement is significant: India has moved from 15th at the first two editions to fourth, while increasing its tally at every successive Games.The challenge now is to sustain that momentum, build a deeper pool of competitive athletes and reduce dependence on a handful of disciplines.For a contingent of just 167 athletes, 114 medals represent more than a record. They mark the latest step in a 16-year transformation of Indian para-sport — one that began with 14 medals in Guangzhou and has now culminated in a historic fourth-place finish in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi- Nagoya. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place. It is the best finish in the country's history at the event.

Article Title: IND A vs NZ A 1st unofficial Test: Devdutt Padikkal, Sai Sudharsan hit back after KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal failures
Article Text:
Devdutt Padikkal (Image credit: X)

Jaiswal, Rahul fall cheaply

Padikkal, Sudharsan put India A back on track

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kamboj, Nabi take three wickets each

Poll Vote & Share your view Should KL Rahul be dropped for the next match based on his performance so far? Yes, he needs a break No, he deserves more chances 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Devdutt Padikkal and Sai Sudharsan helped India A recover from a poor start with an unbeaten 96-run partnership on Day 2 of the first unofficial Test against New Zealand A in Lincoln on Saturday.India A reached 106/2 in their second innings at stumps, trailing New Zealand A by 98 runs. Padikkal was unbeaten on 56 off 89 balls, while Sudharsan scored 39 off 104 balls.The partnership brought some relief to the Indian dressing room after the visitors lost two wickets for just 10 runs. India A had been bowled out for 113 in their first innings, giving New Zealand A a 204-run lead after the hosts scored 317.India A got off to another poor start in their second innings as Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul failed to score big.Jaiswal made just five runs before Simon Keene dismissed him with a short ball. The delivery followed Jaiswal as he tried to move out of its way, hit his glove and went through to wicketkeeper Mitchell Hay.Rahul also had a disappointing outing. After scoring a duck in the first innings, he managed only four runs before losing his wicket. He dragged a delivery from Fraser Sheat onto his stumps while trying to play a ball outside off stump.With India A at 10/2, Padikkal and Sudharsan had the difficult task of rebuilding the innings.Padikkal and Sudharsan showed patience and helped India A recover. The pair added 96 runs without losing another wicket, taking the team to 106/2 by the end of the day.Padikkal hit nine fours in his 89-ball knock and completed his half-century. He was lucky to get another chance during his innings but looked solid for most of his stay at the crease.Sudharsan also played an important role. He found it difficult to play some deliveries, especially when trying to flick the ball towards the leg side. He was also troubled by balls that moved away from him. However, he stayed at the crease and gave Padikkal good support.The pair scored 25 runs in the last 10 overs without losing a wicket, helping India A end the day on a better note.Earlier, India's bowlers tried to keep New Zealand A in check but the hosts still managed to build a big lead.Anshul Kamboj and Auqib Nabi took three wickets each, while Akash Deep claimed two. Washington Sundar and Mukesh Choudhary picked up one wicket each.New Zealand A captain Rhys Mariu scored 76, while Dean Foxcroft made 51 and Kristian Clarke added 42. The hosts were bowled out for 317 in 89.3 overs, taking a 204-run lead.India A ended the day trailing by 98 runs with eight wickets in hand. Padikkal and Sudharsan will look to continue their partnership on Day 3 and help the visitors get closer to the hosts' total.Rain was forecast for the third day and could affect play.
Article Summary: India A reach 106/2 in their second innings at stumps, trailing New Zealand A by 98 runs. Devdutt Padikkal was unbeaten on 56 off 89 balls, while Sai Sudharsan scored 39 off 104 balls. India A had been bowled out for 113 in their first innings, giving New Zealand a 204-run lead.

Article Title: Asian Para Games bronze leaves Suhas Yathiraj hungry for gold amid IAS duties and badminton
Article Text:
Suhas Yathiraj (Image credit: Instagram)

Third Paralympics, one big dream: Gold at LA 2028

Suhas Yathiraj (Image credit: Special arrangement)

IAS officer by day, shuttler by night

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Suhas Yathiraj (Image credit: Instagram)

Lee Chong Wei 's influence

NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.
Article Summary: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. The Indian shuttler lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23- 21, 8-21, 15-21. Suhas has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024.

Article Title: FIFA U15 World Cup 2026: India beat Cameroon 2-1, register second consecutive Group K win
Article Text:
Baku, Oct 25 (IANS) India continued their winning start at the inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup 2026, defeating Cameroon 2-1 in their second Group K match at the Hovsan Competition Complex Pitch 1B on Sunday.

Jenit shines as India withstand Cameroon pressure

Lalremruatfela scores winner as Jenit saves penalty

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India continued their impressive start at the inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup 2026, beating Cameroon 2-1 in their second Group K match on Sunday. The Blue Colts took an early lead through a Cameroon own goal, but Muhammad Sohil Khan’s own goal brought the African side level before the break.Captain R Lalremruatfela scored the winner in the second half, finishing a low cross from Deepak Singh Arambam. Goalkeeper Jenit Ningthoujam played a key role in the victory, making several important saves, including stopping a penalty.With two wins from two matches, India are the only team in Group K to have won both their games so far.India got off to a quick start in rainy conditions when Deepak’s corner in the first minute led to Fareil Ngobo accidentally putting the ball into his own net. Cameroon gradually grew into the game, but India defended well and created chances to extend their lead.Goalkeeper Jenit was particularly impressive, denying several Cameroon attempts, including a dangerous free-kick and a close-range effort. India also came close to scoring through Lalremruatfela, but Cameroon managed to clear the danger.Cameroon eventually equalised in the 20th minute when Ndam Moctar’s cross struck Muhammad Sohil Khan and went into the net.The teams went into the break level at 1-1.India came out with greater purpose after half-time, and substitute Ronandev Aheibam made an immediate impact by winning the ball in midfield. He passed it wide to Deepak, who sent a low cross into the box. Lalremruatfela calmly finished with his left foot in the 27th minute to put India back in front.Cameroon had a chance to equalise after being awarded a penalty for handball, but Jenit came to India’s rescue once again, saving Harouna Abdoulaye’s spot-kick in the 32nd minute.India continued to threaten, with Ronandev testing the Cameroon goalkeeper and Soumojit Sarkar forcing another save from a free-kick. The Blue Colts held their lead until the final whistle, securing their second consecutive win and strengthening their position in Group K.
Article Summary: India beat Cameroon 2-1 in their second Group K match on Sunday. The Blue Colts took an early lead through a Cameroon own goal. Muhammad Sohil Khan’s own goal brought the African side level before the break. Captain R Lalremruatfela scored the winner in the second half.

Article Title: India's para track and field stars lead golden surge at Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Dilip Mahadu Gavit (IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s para-athletes continued to swell the medal tally with a superb haul of gold medals on Thursday, as Shailesh Kumar spearheaded a podium sweep in the men’s high jump T63, Anjanaben Bumbadiya triumphed in the women’s 400m T47, and Dilip Mahadu Gavit secured his second gold of the Games in Nagoya.Defending champion Dharmaraj Solairaj smashed the Asian record in the men’s T44/T62/T64 long jump, while Suvarna Raj clinched gold in the women’s F54 discus throw, underlining the nation’s growing strength across para-athletics disciplines.Shailesh produced a Games-record leap of 1.89m to take the high jump gold. Former Paralympic bronze medallist Varun Bhati claimed silver with a season’s best of 1.84m, while Rahul completed the Indian clean sweep with 1.81m.Bumbadiya clocked 59.97s to win the women’s 400m T47 title, with compatriot Jayanti Behera taking silver in 1:00.65. Thailand’s Sasirawan Inthachot finished third in 1:02.58.Gavit, who had won the men’s 100m T47 gold on Wednesday, added another yellow metal by winning the 400m in 48.27s. Bhavikkumar Bharwad initially finished second in 49.31s but was disqualified for a second lane infringement. Japan’s Kakeru Ishida was consequently upgraded to silver, while Uzbekistan’s Marufjon Murodulloev took bronze.Solairaj, a 32-year-old Tamil Nadu jumper, registered 7.15m in his second attempt to break the Asian record. Malaysia’s Eddy Bernard won silver with 6.34m, while Japan’s Yuma Tamaki secured bronze with 6.89m.Suvarna, 44, delivered a winning discus throw of 15.66m. Iran’s Shahla Hadidi took silver with 15.45m and Vietnam’s Thi Ngoc Thuy Nguyen won bronze with 14.65m. India added further podium finishes through visually impaired Tejalben Damor, who won silver in the women’s 400m T12 in 57.60 seconds after her 200m bronze, and Ravanni Valasanaini, who claimed bronze in the women’s 400m T11 with a personal best of 1:03.64.India has so far won 52 medals from para-athletics, with 18 gold, 16 silver and 18 bronze after the end of Day 4 of the competitions.
Article Summary: Shailesh Kumar leads podium sweep in men's high jump T63. Anjanaben Bumbadiya wins women's 400m T47 title. Dilip Mahadu Gavit secures his second gold of the Games in Nagoya.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Sandeep, Haney strike gold with world-record feats as India hit 100 medals
Article Text:
Sandeep sets T44 world record (Image: ANI)

Sandeep sets world record, Ajay Kumar claims bronze

Haney breaks world record with 60.49m javelin throw

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India reach 100-medal milestone

India's golden run at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games gathered further momentum on Friday as Sandeep and Haney clinched gold medals with world-record performances in their respective events, taking the country's overall medal tally to 100. Sandeep set a new world record in the men's 400m T64, while Haney produced a record-breaking throw in the men's javelin F37/38 final at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium.Sandeep clocked 52.28 seconds to win the men's 400m final, finishing comfortably ahead of Saudi Arabia's Nour Alsana, who secured silver in 53.13 seconds, a season's best. India's Ajay Kumar claimed bronze in 53.61 seconds, setting a Games record, while China's Huang Ruihua finished fourth with a personal-best time of 54.39 seconds.In the men's 400m, athletes from the T44 and T64 classifications competed together. While Sandeep and Alsana belong to the T44 category, Ajay Kumar competes in T64. Both classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments.Haney followed with a world-record throw of 60.49 metres to claim gold in the men's javelin F37/38 event, earning 1,116 Raza points. Iran's Hormoz Seidikazpounji took silver with a personal-best throw of 50.68 metres, earning 1,009 points, while China's Yu Chengjie secured bronze with an Asian-record effort of 53.66 metres and 943 points.The combined F37 and F38 javelin categories are decided using Raza points, which account for the different classifications. This explains why Seidikazpounji finished ahead of Yu despite recording a shorter throw.The double world-record triumph marked another significant milestone for India, whose overall medal tally crossed 100 at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games.
Article Summary: India reach 100-medal milestone at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games. Sandeep and Haney clinch gold medals with world-record performances in their respective events, taking the country's overall medal tally to 100. Haney breaks world record with 60.49m javelin throw.

Article Title: India tour of New Zealand: Red-hot Shikhar Mohan earns India A call-up; set to replace KL Rahul for two fixtures
Article Text:
Shikhar Mohan (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Jharkhand opener Shikhar Mohan has received a maiden India A call-up for the last two four-day matches against New Zealand. The 21-year-old will replace KL Rahul, who will join the ODI squad after playing the first four-day match against New Zealand A, starting on Saturday at Bert Sutcliffe Oval at Lincoln University.The southpaw has continued his red-hot form with back-to-back hundreds in the ongoing Ranji Trophy season. Shikhar smashed 143 against Kerala in Jamshedpur and then scored a match-saving 127 against Maharashtra in Pune.Shikhar's mentor, Ishank Jaggi, a former Jharkhand cricketer, has heaped praise on the youngster, saying the time is absolutely ripe for him to take the next step."It is perfect timing. He is in good form. Scored two centuries in Ranji. Had a great Duleep Trophy final and Irani Trophy as well," Jaggi told TimesofIndia.com.After an excellent debut season in 2025-26, in which he amassed 613 runs at an average of 55.73, including two centuries, he has started the new season in rollicking fashion, smashing 143 in Jharkhand's opening match against Kerala at the Keenan Stadium in Jamshedpur.The southpaw also made some valuable contributions in the Duleep Trophy final for East Zone, scoring 85 and 52 in the two innings, followed by a solid 60 on a green top in Srinagar in the Irani Trophy, playing for Rest of India against defending Ranji Trophy champions Jammu and Kashmir.Jaggi, who is currently coaching the Jharkhand U-23 side, says Shikhar Mohan has been in top form for the past four to five years."Look, he has been in good form for the last four to five years. He has dominated age-group cricket as well. I feel this is a great time for him to have this experience. It will be great exposure for him. He will realise what he needs to add to his game and will come back as a better cricketer," says Jaggi, who has played 90 First Class matches.Jaggi is correct about the southpaw's rich vein of form. Shikhar Mohan enjoyed significant success with the Under-23 side in the Col CK Nayudu Trophy. In the 2023-24 season, he scored 623 runs, including two hundreds and three fifties. He continued his run-scoring spree the following season, scoring 887 runs, which helped him earn a call-up to the senior side.One issue with Shikhar's batting, which the youngster himself has admitted to, is his inability to convert starts into big scores, something he is working on with Jaggi."In my first year of Under-19 cricket, I scored around 550 runs, with most of my scores in the 70s and 80s. The following year, I wanted to focus more and convert those starts into bigger scores," he had told this website."Before facing a ball, I talk to myself. I remind myself to watch the ball and stay focused. That has helped me a lot. Jaggi bhai also helped me with this, especially when he was with the Under-19 team. I started concentrating more and focusing on one ball at a time.That approach has really helped me," he added.Ishank, however, feels the mental block is something even the game's greats have faced."Everyone has gone through that phase. But you have to understand that he is scoring those 70s and 80s consistently, which is no small achievement. He is still raw and can be groomed, and that's why I said this call has come at the right time," he said.Shikhar will travel to New Zealand on October 26 and will link up with the India A squad in Christchurch, where the second four-day game will be played from October 31.
Article Summary: Jharkhand opener Shikhar Mohan has received a maiden India A call-up for the last two four-day matches against New Zealand. The 21-year-old will replace KL Rahul, who will join the ODI squad. The southpaw has continued his red-hot form with back-to-back hundreds in the ongoing Ranji Trophy season.

Article Title: With Brandon Royval setback behind him, Lone’er Kavanagh braces for Ramazan Temirov’s knockout threat at UFC 333
Article Text:
Lone’er Kavanagh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lone’er Kavanagh has not made major changes to his preparation for Ramazan Temirov. The British flyweight says the work has centred on mistakes from his last fight, a submission loss to Brandon Royval in July.“There hasn't been too much change. It's more about learning from the mistakes I made in the last fight,” Kavanagh told TimesofIndia.com ahead of his UFC 333 fight on October 24 at the Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. “I have such a good team around me that we're always evolving and working on the finer details - the little things we need to improve.”Kavanagh, ranked sixth in the UFC flyweight division, faces 10th-ranked Temirov. The fight comes after a year in which he beat former champion Brandon Moreno by unanimous decision in February before losing to Royval in July. Both bouts went beyond the opening round, but ended differently for the 27-year-old.“Both fights have taught me a lot, and I'm going to continue learning from them,” Kavanagh said. “Every fight I have and every mistake I make will teach me something until the day I retire. I think that's the main thing - I'm always learning.”The Moreno fight was a five-round test against a former champion, while Royval submitted Kavanagh with a rear-naked choke in the third round. The latter bout also earned both fighters Fight of the Night honours. Kavanagh now returns to the Octagon against an opponent coming off a first-round knockout.Temirov stopped former flyweight title challenger Steve Erceg in July, extending his winning streak to 12 fights. The Uzbek fighter has a 20-3 professional record, including 12 knockout wins and 11 first-round finishes.“Obviously, Ramazan is very powerful. He likes to come forward and land big shots, and I feel like that works very well for me,” Kavanagh said. “As long as I stay focused and switched on, I'm able to make it a good fight and keep myself safe.”Temirov called out Kavanagh after the Erceg victory. The Englishman, however, sees little reason to read a personal motive into the challenge.“I think it's just a fight that makes sense, right? Obviously, he wants to climb up the rankings, and I was next on the ladder,” Kavanagh said. “So I don't take it personally because I do the same thing. I'm always looking to climb upwards.”The rankings give the bout a clear purpose. Kavanagh is looking to consolidate his position after the Royval defeat, while Temirov has the chance to beat a top-six opponent after his win over Erceg. For Kavanagh, the immediate target is to establish himself as a future title contender.“I think it's a good fight to establish myself as a future title contender,” he said. “He's got a good record and is coming off a good win, so I feel like the winner will be right back at the top.”He is not ready to name a preferred opponent beyond Saturday. Kavanagh said he would speak to his coach and manager after the fight before deciding on his next move.“I'm not too sure yet. I'm very much a one-fight-at-a-time kind of person,” he said. “So, I'll get this one done first, then we'll speak to my coach and my manager and see what's next.”Asked what version of himself fans should expect to see against Temirov, Kavanagh returned to the idea of continued improvement.“The best version of myself - the one that's always improving,” he said. “And, yeah, that's what's going to happen.”UFC 333 will be live on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV.
Article Summary: Lone’er Kavanagh has not made major changes to his preparation for Ramazan Temirov. The British flyweight says the work has centred on mistakes from his last fight, a submission loss to Brandon Royval in July. The fight comes after a year in which he beat former champion Brandon Moreno by unanimous decision.

Qatar will host the final three matches of the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2026, with the tournament culminating in the final on December 16, when defending champions Paris Saint-Germain will take on the FIFA Challenger Cup winners.FIFA has confirmed that the concluding fixtures of the annual club competition will be played on December 9, 12 and 16, bringing together continental champions from across the six confederations in the race for the title. This will be the third consecutive year that Qatar has hosted the final stages, following the 2024 and 2025 editions.The FIFA Derby of the Americas and FIFA Challenger Cup will be staged at Jassim bin Hamad Stadium in Doha, while Ahmad bin Ali Stadium in Al Rayyan will host the final.PSG, who won the competition in Qatar in December 2025, will enter the final as defending champions after Real Madrid lifted the trophy in the inaugural edition under the current format in 2024.The FIFA Derby of the Americas will open the Qatar leg on Wednesday, December 9, with Toluca FC, the Concacaf Champions Cup winners, facing the winners of the 2026 CONMEBOL Libertadores at Jassim bin Hamad Stadium.The victors will return to the same venue on Saturday, December 12, to meet African champions Mamelodi Sundowns FC in the FIFA Challenger Cup.The winner of that contest will secure a place in the final against PSG on Wednesday, December 16.The competition features five single-leg matches in total, with the opening two fixtures taking place at the home stadiums of participating clubs as determined by FIFA rankings. The final three matches will be played in Qatar, with four trophies available across the tournament.The 2026 competition began in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, on August 26, when AFC Champions League winners Al Ahli FC defeated OFC Champions League winners Auckland FC 1-0 in the FIFA African-Asian-Pacific Play-off.CAF Champions League winners Mamelodi Sundowns then beat Al Ahli FC 2-1 in Pretoria, South Africa, on September 19, winning the FIFA African-Asian-Pacific Cup and booking their place in the FIFA Challenger Cup.Sundowns will now await the winner of the Derby of the Americas for a shot at reaching the final.With PSG already assured of a place in the title decider, the three December fixtures in Qatar will determine which clubs from the Americas and Africa progress to challenge the European champions for the 2026 crown.

Article Title: No sponsor, a career-threatening setback and one big dream: Nayanika Sanga’s story
Article Text:
Nayanika Sanga (Insta)

NEW DELHI:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Nayanika Sanga, golf has always been about more than the scorecard. As the 22-year-old from Gurugram prepares to compete at the Women’s Indian Open from Oct 22-25 at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram, she is drawing on lessons learnt over years of competition, international exposure and a difficult comeback from injury. Her approach is simple: concentrate on what she can control, appreciate the opportunity to play and treat every round as a fresh challenge.The philosophy reflects a maturity that has developed through experience. Having travelled abroad for tournaments, including competing in France, Nayanika has learnt to approach the demands of professional golf with greater perspective.“When you play in India, it is like a family. You feel at home and at ease. But when you play outside, the environment is different. People are new, and there can be a language barrier. I think that has made me a little more resilient. When I compete back home now, I feel comfortable because I know the place and the people,” she said.Her journey began when she was five. Her father, who serves in the Navy, wanted her to take up a sport, believing it would help her develop as an individual. She tried squash, tennis and golf, but the response to her natural ability with a club encouraged the family to pursue the latter.Competition soon followed, and the game became a defining part of her life.One of the earliest milestones arrived when she was 11, winning the Kazi Cup at Willingdon Club in Mumbai.“That was definitely a life-changing experience because that was my first win as a child, a big win as a child. Once you start winning, it reinforces that feeling that you want to keep chasing it again and again,” she said.The road since then, however, has not been without setbacks. A wrist injury four years ago came at a particularly difficult time, when she had just turned professional and was playing well. Gratitude journalling became an important part of that process.“When I started playing again, I began focusing on smaller things and feeling grateful that at least today I can play, and tomorrow I can compete. Instead of thinking, ‘I need to win today’, being grateful for the small things in life has definitely helped me,” she said.Physical conditioning has also played a significant role in her return. A professional golfer’s workload extends beyond the hours spent practising and playing. Frequent travel, tournaments scheduled close together and the physical demands of carrying her own bag at overseas events can take a toll. Nayanika credits her strength and conditioning coach, Shaurya Sinha, with helping her rebuild confidence in her body and handle the demands of the circuit.“Because of fitness, I have been a little more resilient to injuries. Other than the injury I had four years ago, I have not had any issues, and I feel my fitness routine is what gets me going every week,” she said.The Women’s Indian Open will present another test. Nayanika regards the DLF Golf and Country Club course as challenging, but prefers to see its demands as an opportunity rather than an obstacle.“I think it is challenging in a fun way. I do not see the course as challenging; rather, every day will be a new challenge there. It will be fun to tackle a new challenge every day,” she said.That outlook also shapes how she approaches a field featuring accomplished players. Rather than becoming preoccupied with the reputations of her opponents, she wants to learn from them while remaining focused on her own performance. She relies more on feel and instinct than data when making decisions on the course, trusting her judgement when she believes her game is in good shape.Nayanika has also witnessed the growth of women’s golf in India. When she first turned professional, she recalled fields of around 30 to 35 players. This year, she said, the numbers have risen to approximately 60 to 62, reflecting greater interest among younger golfers in pursuing the professional route. Lower scores and more opportunities to compete overseas have contributed to the improving standard.Yet the growth of the game has not removed one of its persistent challenges: funding. Despite competing abroad and continuing to develop as a professional, she is still looking for a sponsor. Coming from a middle-class family, with her father serving in the Navy, she knows the financial demands of sustaining a career on tour.“It has been tough. My parents have sacrificed so much for me, and they continue to do so to support me,” she said.Her grandparents also travelled with her to tournaments when she was younger, stepping in whenever her father’s work commitments prevented him from accompanying her. Nayanika acknowledges their contribution.Away from golf, time with friends and playing badminton help her switch off from the constant demands of professional competition. She also looks up to Diksha Dagar and Aditi Ashok whose achievements have out Indian golf on the global map.Nayanika hopes her journey can encourage more young girls to pursue sport, particularly in a society where conventional career choices often dominate expectations.“If you fall in love with a sport, there is nothing better than that feeling. Parents should be willing to explore sporting opportunities when their children show interest and ability,” she said.As she heads into the Women’s Indian Open, her ambitions remain tied to the fundamentals she has learnt through experience: trust her instincts, stay patient and focus on the next shot. For a golfer who has learnt to find perspective in adversity, the challenge is not simply to compete against a strong field, but to keep moving forward, one round at a time.
Article Summary: Nayanika Sanga, 22, will compete at the Women’s Indian Open from Oct 22-25 at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram. Her approach is simple: concentrate on what she can control, appreciate the opportunity to play and treat every round as a fresh challenge.

Article Title: Three Jharkhand players in India squad for historic lawn bowls series against New Zealand
Article Text:
(From left) Sunil Bahadur, Dinesh Kumar and Reshma Kumari

Kolkata: Three players from Jharkhand will be part of India’s four-member lawn bowls squad for a historic three-Test series against New Zealand in Nov, part of the centenary celebrations of sporting ties between the two countries.Lawn bowls is one of the only four sports, alongside cricket, hockey and football, selected for the centenary programme.2022 Commonwealth Games silver medallists Dinesh Kumar and Sunil Bahadur and rising player Reshma Kumari, all from Jharkhand, have been selected alongside Arjuna Awardee and Commonwealth Games gold medallist Pinki Singh for the series, scheduled from Nov 16-18 in Auckland.“This is a very important event for us because only four sports are taking part in the centenary celebrations. On the days we are playing, no other sport will be taking place, which means we will receive exclusive coverage,” Bowling Federation of India president Ravi Bengani told TOI in an exclusive interview on Thursday.India will play three Test matches over three days, with each Test comprising five matches — men’s pairs, women’s pairs, mixed fours, mixed pairs 1 and mixed pairs 2.The New Zealand series is part of a broader international exposure programme the federation has put in place as it begins preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.A 12-member Indian contingent will travel to Malaysia later this month for a World Bowls-sanctioned tournament, while another group will compete in an invitational event in Hong Kong, where Indian players won bronze medals last year.The federation’s confidence has also received a boost from Putul Sonowal’s recent podium finish at the Champion of Champions event, a first for an Indian player at the prestigious competition.“We have decided to participate in as many World Bowls-sanctioned events as possible. International exposure is crucial if we want to bridge the gap with the leading nations,” Bengani said.The federation is also planning to strengthen its support structure through its partnership with Bowls New Zealand. Bengani revealed that India currently does not have a dedicated national coach, making the proposed knowledge-sharing programme particularly significant.“We have signed an agreement with Bowls New Zealand and now we will have more exchange programmes. We will bring their coaches and technical officials to India and provide our players with greater exposure and expertise,” Bengani said.The plans have gained momentum following the federation’s recognition by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports earlier this year, a move expected to improve funding and access to high-performance support.As far as the 2030 Commonwealth Games are concerned, the federation has set ambitious targets. “I’m committing to at least four gold medals for India in 2030. Personally, I feel we can win even more if we continue on the current path,” Bengani said.With a packed international calendar, plans to bring in New Zealand coaches and technical experts, and Ahmedabad 2030 on the horizon, the federation believes Indian lawn bowls is entering its most ambitious phase yet.
Article Summary: Lawn bowls is one of the only four sports, alongside cricket, hockey and football, selected for the centenary programme. India will play three Test matches over three days, with each Test comprising five matches. The series is part of a broader international exposure programme the federation has put in place as it begins preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.

Article Title: EFI mess costs Indian riders global stage, FEI ban from Dec 1
Article Text:
Equestrian Federation of India

New Delhi:

Yet another tale of administrative chaos and athletes paying the price. Caught in a prolonged governance crisis at the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), Indian riders now face a ban from international competitions, with their sporting futures hanging in the balance. The latest setback comes at a time when the govt is pushing to bring more international events to India and widen Indian athletes’ exposure to global competition.The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) has decided to suspend the EFI from Dec 1 over prolonged governance irregularities and failure to hold fresh elections, effectively shutting Indian riders, officials, trainers and horses out of international events. TOI is in possession of FEI’s Oct 15 letter confirming the decision, which was taken at the international body's board meeting on Oct 13.Explaining its move, the FEI said the EFI’s prolonged governance crisis had reached a tipping point. “The absence of elections to date to elect a new Executive Committee, has resulted in a prolonged governance and leadership irregularity that is no longer sustainable,” the letter by FEI Governance Director Francisco Lima stated.The crisis follows the Delhi high court’s dissolution of the EFI executive committee in Feb 2026. Its elected tenure had expired in Sept 2023, while fresh elections remain pending nine months after the court’s intervention. The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) constituted an ad hoc committee on March 27 to oversee the federation and facilitate the electoral process.While acknowledging the committee’s Sept 27 submission and its work, the FEI said elections were expected by Jan 31, 2027. However, the suspension will be reviewed only after the polls are held and evaluated by the international body.The consequences are sweeping. Citing its statutes, the FEI said the EFI “may not attend or be represented at any session or meeting of any FEI body, nor may it organise international events.” More damagingly, athletes, officials, trainers and horses “may not participate in international events organised by the FEI or any other national federation, whether under the Indian flag or the FEI flag.”With the suspension taking effect before the stated election deadline, Indian riders risk losing crucial international competition opportunities. Their return will depend on the completion of elections and the FEI’s subsequent evaluation, leaving athletes caught in a governance crisis they did not create.
Article Summary: The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) has decided to suspend the EFI from Dec 1 over prolonged governance irregularities and failure to hold fresh elections. Indian riders now face a ban from international competitions, with their sporting futures hanging in the balance. The latest setback comes at a time when the govt is pushing to bring more international events to India and widen Indian athletes' exposure to global competition.

Article Title: SA vs AUS: Steve Smith cleared of concussion after helmet blow, returns to field in Durban Test

Former Australia captain Steve Smith has been cleared of concussion and resumed fielding duties on the fifth day of the first Test against South Africa at Kingsmead in Durban on Tuesday, after undergoing a series of clinical assessments following a blow to the helmet.The 37-year-old batter was struck by a short-pitched delivery from Anrich Nortje during Australia's second innings. Smith attempted to duck under the ball but misjudged its trajectory as it failed to rise as much as he expected.Although he continued batting after the incident, scoring 27 off 41 balls before being caught at long-on off Simon Harmer, Smith did not take the field when South Africa began their second innings on Monday. Michael Neser served as his substitute fielder during that session.However, Smith returned to the field on Tuesday morning after being cleared under Cricket Australia's concussion protocols. He was stationed in the slip cordon when South Africa resumed their chase and subsequently took a catch to dismiss Kyle Verreynne off Matt Renshaw's bowling."Steve Smith has undergone a series of clinical assessments over the past 24 hours in accordance with Cricket Australia’s concussion protocols and has been cleared to take the field this morning," Cricket Australia said in a statement.The incident brought back memories of Smith's previous concussion scare during the 2019 Ashes in England, when he was struck on the head by fast bowler Jofra Archer and forced to miss part of a Test match.Smith's return to the field came after medical assessments over the preceding 24 hours, with Australia following the prescribed protocols before allowing the experienced batter to resume his duties.His presence was a boost for Australia as they pushed for victory in the series opener, with South Africa mounting a determined resistance on the final day.South Africa resumed at 102/4 on Tuesday, needing another 319 runs to win. They reached 166/6 by lunch after Australia struck twice to strengthen their grip on the contest.Opener Aiden Markram led the home side's resistance, remaining unbeaten on 69 at the interval alongside Marco Jansen on seven. The pair had to rebuild after Wiaan Mulder's patient 69-run fifth-wicket partnership with Markram ended when Josh Hazlewood had Mulder caught behind by Alex Carey.Part-time spinner Matt Renshaw then dismissed Verreynne, who made just one before edging a reckless shot to Smith at slip.Renshaw has been Australia's standout performer with the bat, having scored 190 in the first innings and 82 in the second, before adding two wickets to his match contribution.Australia needed four more wickets at lunch to seal victory in the opening Test. The second Test of the series is scheduled to begin in Gqeberha on Sunday.
Article Summary: Steve Smith cleared of concussion after blow to the helmet. Former Australia captain was struck by short-pitched delivery from Anrich Nortje. Smith took a catch to dismiss Kyle Verreynne off Matt Renshaw's bowling. Australia needed four more wickets at lunch to seal victory in the opening Test.

Article Title: 'Not once have people really mentioned Matt Kuhnemann': Usman Khawaja on Australia’s Test Selection dilemma

Khawaja backs Kuhnemann for final Test

Khawaja weighs in on Australia’s batting options

Former Australia opener Usman Khawaja has urged selectors to consider left-arm spinner Matt Kuhnemann for the decisive final Test against South Africa in Cape Town.With the series now level at 2-1, Australia need to get their team selection right after suffering a heavy defeat in the previous match.Australia left experienced spinner Nathan Lyon out of the Gqeberha Test and picked fast bowler Scott Boland instead. Boland performed well, taking five wickets, but Australia’s decision to play without a frontline spinner backfired as South Africa won by an innings and 31 runs.Khawaja believes Kuhnemann deserves a chance, especially because South Africa have several right-handed batters. The left-arm spinner has played five Tests and already taken a five-wicket haul. Although he has not played a Test since February 2025, he impressed during Australia’s tour of Sri Lanka, finishing the two-match series with 16 wickets.“We’ve talked about Boland and Lyon (in the second Test), and not once have people really mentioned Kuhnemann. He is a terrific bowler, a Test bowler. He has a Test five-fa, and done really well for Australia when he’s played,” Khawaja told foxsports.com.au.He explained that Kuhnemann could trouble right-handed batters by making the ball spin away from them, much like South African spinner Simon Harmer troubled Australia’s left-handers.“I know Nathan Lyon’s the ‘GOAT’, and there’s nothing against the GOAT! This is purely based on the fact the South Africans have so many right-handers in their team. I think Kuhnemann deserves to be talked about,” Khawaja added.Australia also face questions about their batting order ahead of the series decider. Selectors must decide whether Nic Maddinson should continue opening, where Marnus Labuschagne should bat and how to fit Cam Green back into the team as he nears a return from injury.Khawaja believes Maddinson could be more effective in the middle order, where he can face spin bowling rather than handle the difficult task of opening the innings.“No discredit to Nic Maddinson. I think Maddinson is terrific. I actually would have put him in the middle order at the start of the series, purely based on the fact the opening is so hard of a gap to fill,” Khawaja concluded.

Article Title: Watch: MS Dhoni has a message for younger generations like GenZ and Gen Alpha

Former India captain MS Dhoni has shared an important message for Gen Z and Gen Alpha, urging young people to stay physically active and take better care of their health. Speaking at an event alongside renowned writer Javed Akhtar, Dhoni focused on how modern lifestyles, long hours of sitting and unhealthy eating habits can affect young people in the long run.The discussion began with a question about what advice they would give to younger generations, who are dealing with difficult situations and emotional challenges. While Akhtar praised the younger generation, Dhoni chose to highlight their physical well-being.Javed Akhtar said today’s young people are better than previous generations in several ways. He admitted that his generation was often caught up in its own beliefs and principles, while young people today are showing stronger moral values.Akhtar suggested that older generations should learn from the youth instead of assuming they always have the answers.Dhoni, however, said he still had some advice to offer, particularly when it came to health and everyday habits.Dhoni explained that earlier generations naturally moved around more, which helped them digest food and maintain a healthier lifestyle. Today, people can travel from home to work using services, spend most of the day sitting in an office and then return home by car.He warned that this lack of physical activity, combined with the growing popularity of fast food, could lead to health problems later in life.Dhoni also pointed out that sugary and fried foods can be especially harmful when people do not get enough exercise.His advice to young people was simple: make physical activity and sports part of their daily routine. Even if an inactive lifestyle does not cause immediate problems, its effects may become more noticeable after the age of 30.The former India captain’s message was a reminder that staying healthy requires consistent effort.Along with managing modern-day pressures, young people should prioritise exercise, make healthier food choices and develop habits that support their long-term well-being.
Article Summary: Dhoni spoke at an event alongside renowned writer Javed Akhtar. He urged young people to stay physically active and take better care of their health. NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games with their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals as the week-long continental competition concluded with a closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday.Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal led the Indian contingent as flag-bearers at the ceremony, marking the end of a landmark campaign in which the country's para-athletes delivered historic victories, world-record performances and podium sweeps across disciplines.India finished fourth in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 Hangzhou Games.Held in Japan for the first time, the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games brought together around 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions. The competition featured 18 sports, with more than 20 world records reportedly set during the seven-day event.China topped the medal table with 435 medals, including 207 gold, while hosts Japan finished second with 186 medals — 64 gold, 60 silver and 62 bronze.Uzbekistan emerged as the third-ranked nation, collecting 145 medals, including 45 gold.India's fourth-place finish was particularly significant given the size of its contingent. A total of 168 para-athletes represented the country at Aichi-Nagoya, compared with 309 at the previous edition in Hangzhou.President Droupadi Murmu congratulated the Indian contingent on its record performance, saying the achievement reflected the athletes' hard work, perseverance and self-belief.In a post on X, Murmu said the unprecedented medal haul would inspire young people to dream big, work with dedication and remain positive in the face of challenges. She also extended her congratulations to the entire Indian contingent.Para athletics was India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. Para badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze.India also won 11 medals in para swimming, seven in para table tennis, six in para archery and five in para shooting. The contingent added two medals each in para judo and para powerlifting.The closing ceremony brought together athletes, officials and dignitaries to mark the conclusion of the Games. Asian Paralympic Committee president Majid Rashed declared the event closed, highlighting the growing strength of para sport across Asia and its role in building a more inclusive society.Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also praised the athletes' determination, teamwork and sportsmanship, describing their performances as a reminder of the “profound beauty” of para sports.The Asian Para Games began in Guangzhou, China, in 2010, evolving from the Far East and South Pacific Games Federation for the Disabled. The Aichi-Nagoya edition was the fifth staging of the event, with Doha, Qatar, scheduled to host the sixth in 2030.For India, the closing ceremony marked the end of a historic campaign — one that raised the country's medal benchmark and showcased the depth and growing strength of its para-sport movement.

Article Title: India script history with best-ever haul of 114 medals as nine golds cap golden day at Asian Para Games

NEW DELHI: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games, registering their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals, including 30 gold, after a record-breaking final-day flourish in Aichi-Nagoya on Friday.India collected nine gold medals on the day — their biggest single-day haul of the ongoing edition — with champions emerging from badminton, archery, shooting and athletics. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023.The achievement was particularly significant as India competed with a contingent of 168 athletes, nearly half the size of the squad that represented the country in Hangzhou.India remained fourth in the standings at the end of its campaign, although the final positions could change after a few remaining events on Saturday.Athletics remained India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals, 12 more than at the previous edition. On Friday, however, the spotlight was shared with a superb badminton campaign and gold-winning performances in shooting and archery. Star javelin thrower Sumit Antil led an Indian 1-2-3 finish in the men's F42-44/61-64 combined event . The reigning Paralympic and world champion threw 72.46m to defend his title, while Mahendra Gurjar took silver with 59.03m and Sandip Sanjay Sargar claimed bronze with 64.48m. Gurjar finished ahead of Sargar on Raza points, which determine rankings in combined-classification events.Pranav Soorma added another gold in the men's club throw F51, defending his title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m. Dharambir secured bronze with 27.71m.Sandeep delivered a world-record performance in the men's 400m T64, clocking 52.28 seconds for gold. India's Ajay Kumar also reached the podium, winning bronze in a Games-record time of 53.61 seconds.Haney produced another world record, throwing 60.49m to win the men's javelin F37/38 title. India also picked up silver medals through Nimisha Chakkungalparambil in the women's long jump T47 and Parmod Bijarnia in the men's 1500m T46, where he clocked 4:09.65.India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar and Games debutant Naveen Sivakumar.Nitesh defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles SL3 final. He later added a silver medal in mixed doubles SL3-SU5 alongside Thulasimathi Murugesan.Naveen, meanwhile, defeated Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 to win the men's singles SL4 title. Thulasimathi enjoyed a memorable campaign of her own , combining with Manasi Joshi to win gold in women's doubles SL3-SU5. The Indian pair beat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final.The 24-year-old also secured silver in women's singles SU5 after losing 18-21, 11-21 to Yang in the final, completing a three-medal haul.Shooter Mona Agarwal added another golden chapter to India's campaign, shattering the world record to win the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 title with a score of 357.5 points.The 38-year-old had earlier won the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold with a Games-record score of 250.0 points, edging compatriot Avani Lekhara, who took silver with 249.6.Mona's latest triumph gave her a second gold of the Games and further underlined her standing among India's leading para-shooters. She had also secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota earlier this year.In archery, Paralympic champion Harvinder Singh teamed up with debutant Vijay Sundi to win the men's recurve doubles gold, defeating China's Yun Duo and Zhao Lixue 5-1 in the final.India's women's recurve doubles pair of Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan settled for silver after losing 0-6 to China's Gao Zihan and Wang Xueqian.India's swimmers also exceeded expectations, finishing the Games with 11 medals, including three silver. Himanshu Nandal completed a hat-trick of bronze medals by finishing third in the men's 100m freestyle S11. The 22-year-old, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 1:05.90, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita (58.22) and China's Chuanzhen Sun (58.70).Nandal had earlier won bronze in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. Ravi Budigina also finished with three medals, comprising two silver and one bronze.With nine gold medals on Friday and a record overall haul of 114, India signed off from its Asian Para Games campaign with its most successful performance at the continental event, surpassing the benchmark set in Hangzhou three years ago.

The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023. India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar.

NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a golden double in para-athletics at the Asian Para Games on Friday, with star javelin thrower Sumit Antil leading a podium sweep and Pranav Soorma defending his title in the men's club throw F51 event.Antil successfully defended his gold in the men's javelin throw F42-44/61-64 combined event, while Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar completed an all-Indian podium finish. Soorma, meanwhile, added another gold to his collection with a Games-record performance in the club throw.The results added to India's medal haul as the country's para-athletes continued to deliver strong performances in Aichi-Nagoya.The 28-year-old Antil, a two-time Paralympic gold medallist and world record holder, produced a best throw of 72.46m in his second attempt to claim gold.Although he could not surpass his personal best, Antil was comfortably ahead of the field while competing in the F64 classification. He had won gold at the 2023 Asian Para Games with a then-world-record throw of 73.29m before improving the mark to 74.82m in May this year.Gurjar secured silver with a throw of 59.03m, while Sargar took bronze with an effort of 64.48m.Despite Sargar recording the longer distance, Gurjar finished ahead because of his superior Raza points score, which is used to determine rankings in combined events involving athletes from different classifications.The F42, F44, F62 and F64 categories are combined in certain field events, including javelin and discus throw, to create a larger and more competitive field. The classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments, with some competing without prostheses and others using them.Soorma continued India's gold rush by successfully defending his men's club throw F51 title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m.The Indian had won gold in the same event at the previous edition of the Asian Para Games and claimed silver at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.South Korea's Jiwon Jung took silver with a personal-best throw of 28.40m, while Dharamvir secured bronze with 27.71m to give India another double podium finish.The F51 classification is for athletes with significant movement limitations affecting the trunk, legs and hands, with varying degrees of impairment in arm movement. Competitors perform their throws from a seated position.With Antil leading a historic Indian sweep in the javelin and Soorma retaining his title, India's para-athletes delivered another memorable day in Aichi-Nagoya.

NEW DELHI: Double gold medallists Mona Agarwal and Nishad Kumar will be India's flag-bearers at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, following outstanding campaigns in shooting and para-athletics.Both athletes won two gold medals each at the continental event, with Mona producing a record-breaking performance in shooting and Nishad excelling in the high jump and long jump.Their selection as flag-bearers recognises their achievements as India prepare to bring the Games to a close.The 38-year-old Mona opened India's medal account in shooting by winning gold in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event with a Games-record score of 250.0 points. Article Title: Who is Himanshu Nandal? The para-swimmer who won a hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games in Japan
Article Text:
Himanshu Nandal (PTI Photo)

Who is Himanshu Nandal?

From Paris Paralympics qualification to Asian Para Games medals

NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.
Article Summary: Himanshu Nandal completes hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games 2026. The 22-year-old finished third in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday. Nandal is the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.

India's Thulasimathi Murugesan added another medal to her growing collection at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, settling for silver in the women's singles SU5 badminton event after losing to China's Yang Qiuxia in the final on Friday. The 24-year-old, who won silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, went down 18-21, 11-21 against the Chinese shuttler at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium.However, Thulasimathi's campaign is far from over, with the Indian still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events. The Indian had produced a fighting performance in the semi-finals, rallying from a game down to defeat compatriot and World No. 1 Manisha Ramdass 19-21, 21-15, 21-13 and book her place in the final.The silver medal adds to Thulasimathi's impressive record in para-badminton, following her breakthrough performance at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, where she finished runner-up in the women's singles SU5 category.Thulasimathi will have two more chances to finish her campaign on a high.She has partnered Nitesh Kumar to reach the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, where the Indian duo will face Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.The Indians booked their place in the final after overcoming China's Li Mingpan and Xiao Zuxian in a hard-fought 42-minute semi-final. Her silver medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympics marked a major milestone in her career, while her performances at the Asian Para Games have further strengthened her standing on the international stage.She trains in Hyderabad under coaches Pullela Gopichand and Irfan Sait while pursuing a degree in veterinary science at Namakkal. In recognition of her achievements in para-badminton, including her Paralympic success, she was also honoured with the Arjuna Award.
